title: The two independent readings of where the three-storey Building B sits on lot 70 of block 7334 (215-16 Northern Boulevard, Queens) under Z1 (lot 70 alone) and how its floor area divides, written into the R6B reference cases as one case: the plate as zoning floor area per storey, the footprint on the printed-tax-map basis reconciled with the plate, the placement and offsets on that basis with the city-map (GIS) outline as a conflict check only, the lot coverage and rear yard as far as both readings take them, and the area allocation at the one stated 60 percent apartment-area share - a value only where both readings agree on the same basis
work_order_table: D-094 R043, R044, R076, R082, R091, R092; work order D-094 v3, task M5-T177; the footprint, placement and area allocation of Building B worked independently from source facts and quoted law before the report, the drawing (M5-T173) and the engine (M5-T172) consume it
summary: The footprint, placement and area allocation of the three-storey Building B (20,150 sq ft zoning floor area, 10-ft floor-to-floor) on lot 70 of block 7334, read independently in step P8 by two AI helpers working alone from a sealed folder (the 189 pinned law captures without their notes, the block-7334 lot outlines, the DCM centrelines, the PLUTO rows of lots 70 and 1, the printed tax-map labels, the zoning of lot 70, the stated facts of Building B and the stated measure, and eighteen answers settled by earlier readings - the earlier footprint answer real-building-b left out on purpose), with no access to the program, the repository or the web. It records the plate as zoning floor area per storey (20,150 / 3 = 6,716.67), the footprint on the printed-tax-map basis (100.76 x 66.66 = 6,716.66) reconciled with the plate within the readers' +/- 0.5 sq ft, the placement and offsets under Z1 on that basis with the city-map (GIS) outline used only as a conflict check, the lot coverage (maximum by portion) and the rear yard as far as both readings take them, and the area allocation at the one stated 60 percent apartment-area share. A value or figure is recorded only where both readings give it on the same words and the same basis; every disagreement or unresolved basis stays not settled, naming both readings and the kind of its gap (a missing fact about the property, or unresolved law). The placement is an illustration, not a design; the plate is zoning floor area per storey, no gross-up, exclusions or wall-thickness conversion worked, and the physical floor plate is not checked. No value comes from a program run; no human verdict is entered; a tax lot is not a zoning lot; every quantity carries exactly one of the nine measurement bases and no two bases are mixed in one figure.
what_it_is_worth: Read independently by two AI helpers, each working alone from the sealed step-P8 folder (reading 1 a geospatial-engineer, reading 2 a scenario-optimization-engineer); their agreement alone is not proof. It is a draft reading of the law and an illustrative placement by an AI helper, not professionally reviewed, and is not a statement that anything complies, is buildable, is optimal or is feasible. A second AI read the same sealed folder and worked the same questions. Where the two readings differ, where one says not known, or where the captured text does not settle a point, the row says so and names both readings and the kind of its gap. The placement, the lot coverage and the rear yard stay conditional on the measurement basis, the zoning lot (Z1) and the neighbouring lots' records, which no reading had.
what_it_does_not_establish: It records a value or figure only where both readings agree on the same words and the same basis; where they differ, where one says not known, or where the captured text does not settle a point, the row says so, names both readings and states the kind of its gap.

The placement is an illustration on the printed-tax-map basis under Z1 (lot 70 alone), not a design and not a dwelling layout; no row reads as 'complies', 'buildable', 'optimal' or 'feasible', and no human verdict is entered.

The plate is zoning floor area per storey; no gross-up, exclusions or wall-thickness conversion is worked, and the physical floor plate is not checked; the footprint figure and the plate are separate quantities each on its own exact recompute, reconciled within the readers' +/- 0.5 sq ft and never forced into one figure.

The city-map (GIS) outline is used only as a conflict check; the two bases are never mixed in one figure and no reading chooses between them; the lot coverage (whole lot) and the rear yard stay not known; a tax lot is not a zoning lot.

Every quantity carries exactly one of the nine measurement bases and no two bases are mixed in one figure; no value comes from a program run; agreement between two AI readings is not proof; it is not a professional or legal determination.

checked_by: A second, independent AI (a scenario-optimization-engineer) read the same sealed folder and worked the same questions (reading 2: provenance/return-independent-hand-calculation-18.md). Agreement between two AI answers alone is not proof.

citations.title: Maximum lot coverage in R6 through R12 Districts
citations.quote: the maximum #residential# #lot coverage# for #interior lots# or #through lots# shall be 80 percent and the maximum #residential# #lot coverage# for #corner lots# shall be 100 percent.

citations.title: Definition: corner lot (the corner portion)
citations.quote: The portion of such #zoning lot# subject to the regulations for #corner lots# is that portion bounded by the intersecting #street line# and lines parallel to and 100 feet from each intersecting #street line#. Any remaining portion of a #corner lot# shall be subject to the regulations for a #through lot# or for an #interior lot#, whichever is applicable.

rows.why_applies: ZR 23-362(a) sets the maximum residential lot coverage (80 percent for interior or through lots, 100 percent for corner lots); the ZR 12-10 corner-lot definition fixes which portion of a corner lot is the corner portion and which is left for interior or through treatment.

It is not a single whole-lot percentage (see lot-coverage-whole-lot).

rows.why_applies: ZR 23-344 modifies the rear-yard requirement on corner lots; its (a), (b) and (c) turn on the measurement basis, the short-dimension question and the adjoining lot-line kind, which the readers could not fix for lot 70 under Z1.

Both readings carry the settled step-p7 reading short-block-rear-yard#real-lot-z1-rear-yard, which is not known: on the street-line/tax-map basis the Northern Boulevard frontage is read as a short dimension of a block, so ZR 23-344(b) waives the rear yard within 100 feet of the Northern Boulevard street line; on the centreline basis the result rests on ZR 23-344(a) (no rear yard within 100 feet of the roughly 90-degree corner), the settled no-rear-lot-line finding and ZR 23-344(c) for the strip beyond 100 feet. The stated placement is only 66.66 feet deep from Northern Boulevard, so it lies within 100 feet of that street line; but the building spans the full frontage and sits on the side lot line opposite 215 Place, the portion of which beyond 100 feet of the 215 Place street line is deemed a rear lot line (ZR 23-344(c)), and whether the building may touch there turns on the adjoining zoning lot's lot-line kind. KIND OF GAP: unresolved law (the governing measurement basis, see gis-conflict-check) and a missing fact about the property (the adjoining zoning lot's lot-line kind, from a survey, a deed or the neighbouring lots' records). No unconditional 'no rear yard' is recorded: every reading above names its basis and its conditions and quotes ZR 23-344.
